content.intended_use: A precise distance-reduction witness with finite original-oracle accounting.

dependencies: Lemmas 4.1–4.4, fully located and read in this role
map: Lemma 4.1 obtains Taylor and Jacobian remainders using segment integration, requiring only C^(p-1) plus Lipschitz highest derivative.

Lemma 4.2 supplies a unique model solution and genuine normal. In the affine hull, sym DM_x(z)>=Lp||z-x||^(p-1)I/(p-1)!; integration gives strict monotonicity. Compactness gives existence, continuity and the total measurable extension described in the source.
Lemma 4.4 gives the energy inequality using the projection characterization and the genuine model normal.
Proposition 4.5 sums that inequality, bounds the accumulated step weights by convexity, and uses the explicit equation (4.11) count to obtain r/2 distance.

proofs.full_local_argument: Use the exact model existence and genuine normal furnished by Lemmas 4.1–4.2. For s=y-x and E=G(y)-Gbar_x(y), v=G(y)+n=E-beta||s||^(p-1)s. If s=0, Gbar_x(x)=G(x), so -G(x) is a normal and x is the unique solution. Otherwise lambda=(beta||s||^(p-1))^(-1), lambda v=-s+lambda E and ||lambda E||<=||s||/(2p)<=||s||/2. Projection xplus=Pi_X(x-lambda G(y)) gives, for every u in X, 2lambda<G(y),y-u><=||x-u||^2-||xplus-u||^2-||xplus-x||^2+2lambda<G(y),y-xplus>. Since <n,y-xplus>>=0, replacing G(y) by v in the last term is an upper bound. Put a=xplus-x and b=y-xplus=s-a. Then -||a||^2+2<-s+lambda E,b>=-||s||^2-||b||^2+2<lambda E,b><=-||s||^2+||lambda E||^2<=-3||s||^2/4. With u=z_star, the VI condition and strong monotonicity give <G(y),y-z_star>>=mu||y-z_star||^2. Sum for T nonzero steps from w: 2mu sum_i lambda_i||y_i-z_star||^2+(3/4)sum_i||s_i||^2<=||w-z_star||^2<=r^2. Convexity of t^(-(p-1)/2) yields sum_i||s_i||^(-(p-1))>=T[(sum_i||s_i||^2)/T]^(-(p-1)/2)>=(3/4)^((p-1)/2)T^((p+1)/2)/r^(p-1). Consequently Lambda=sum_i lambda_i>=(3/4)^((p-1)/2)T^((p+1)/2)/(b_p Lp r^(p-1)). The weighted average ybar lies in X by convexity, and Jensen gives ||ybar-z_star||^2<=sum_i lambda_i||y_i-z_star||^2/Lambda<=r^2/(2mu Lambda). The stated maximum/ceiling count ensures T^((p+1)/2)>=2b_p(4/3)^((p-1)/2)Lp r^(p-1)/mu, so Lambda>=2/mu and ||ybar-z_star||^2<=r^2/4. Each nonzero step uses two queries; an early zero step uses only its center jet. Thus at most 2T queries suffice. This proves a distance statement only.

assumptions: G is C^(p-1) on an open neighborhood of X and ||D^(p-1)G(u)-D^(p-1)G(v)||op<=Lp||u-v|| on X.
<G(u)-G(v),u-v>>=mu||u-v||^2 for all u,v in X; hence its VI solution is unique.
Exact feasible oracle jets through D^(p-1)G; exact internal projections and solutions of known Taylor-model VIs, using the original X.
statement.conclusion: Algorithm 1 returns a point in X within distance r/2 of z_star using at most 2T_p(r,mu) original-oracle queries. If y=x is encountered, that exact VI solution may be returned earlier. The bound is O_p(1+(Lp r^(p-1)/mu)^(2/(p+1))). No tangent-residual estimate at the final average follows from this statement.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Finite-dimensional Euclidean R^d; known nonempty compact convex original X with diam(X)<=D. Multilinear norm is sup ||T[u1,...,uj]|| over unit inputs. N_X(x)={n:<n,u-x><=0 for all u in X}. z_star solves 0 in G(z_star)+N_X(z_star). Algorithm 1 uses Gbar_x(y)=sum_{j=0}^{p-1}D^jG(x)[y-x]^j/j!, b_p=2p/p!, beta=b_p Lp=2Lp/(p-1)!, equation (4.1), lambda=(beta||y-x||^(p-1))^(-1), projected extragradient updates and the lambda-weighted average.
statement.parameter_domains: d>=1; fixed integer p>=2; D,Lp,mu,r>0. T_p(r,mu)=max{1,ceil([2b_p(4/3)^((p-1)/2)Lp r^(p-1)/mu]^(2/(p+1)))}.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every admissible G and all listed parameters satisfying these conditions, deterministic Algorithm 1 obeys the conclusion. No random seed or average-case qualification is used.
